P01-006.boundary_rationale: Onset: 3:16 carries the book's first strict word-event formula, וַיְהִ֕י מִקְצֵ֖ה שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Ezek.3.16) (“At the end of seven days, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying” (web:Ezek.3.16)), a hard seam, since a strict word-event opens a new oracle and no unit runs across one (3:16 is one of the 39 strict-form verses and one of the 48 in the first-person family). A pe is recorded after this verse; this witness's section marks carry no intra-verse position, so no claim is made about whether the mark falls before or after 3:17's watchman charge, צֹפֶ֥ה נְתַתִּ֖יךָ לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Ezek.3.17) (“I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.3.17)). A samekh follows 3:19, between the wicked-man case (3:18-19) and the righteous-man case (3:20-21); disclosed as an internal paragraph mark, not a unit cut, since both cases are one paired illustration of the same watchman charge and no fresh onset device stands at 3:20. Close: 3:21, at the second samekh, before the hand-of-YHWH reopens the scene at 3:22.

P01-007.device_notes: Category deviation disclosed: this span also carries commission_narrative texture (the muteness charge proper runs 3:24-3:27 inside this vision-opened scene); labelled vision_report because the unit's onset device is the hand-of-YHWH construct at 3:22. Paseq at 3:27 occurs twice (double occurrence on one verse), disclosed count-only, single-witness. The ropes word shared by 3:25 and 4:8 is disclosed as continuity across the 3:27/4:1 seam; it argues for the closeness of the two units, while the refrain close at 3:27 and the sub-onset at 4:1 keep the seam between them. The witness records a samekh after MT 3:21 (single witness), the mark this unit's onset can claim from its own side.

Inside the span a samekh follows MT 4:12 (single witness); the unit does not cut there because the food-rationing act begun at 4:9 continues without a fresh 'son of man' address or messenger formula reopening the speech. A further samekh stands after MT 4:14 (single witness) inside the span; no cut is made there either, since 4:15's concession is Yahweh's reply within the same rationing scene, not a fresh address. A samekh also follows MT 4:15 (single witness), inside the span as well; no cut is made there, because the address at 4:16 intensifies the rationing act rather than restarting it.

P01-009.device_notes: Whole-chapter span, 17-verse unit, over the 7-10 verse target; disclosed as over the target rather than forced into an unsupported internal cut, as at oshb:Ezek.4.1-4.17, since no refrain-plus-fresh-onset pair stands anywhere inside 5:1-5:17 to license a shorter cut. Paseq at 5:1 and 5:7 disclosed count-only, single-witness. Marks after 5:4 (pe), 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 (samekh) and 5:10 (pe) are disclosed as intra-row, single-witness texture. Three of those five marks coincide with a formula onset on the verse following them. The pe after 5:4 stands before the messenger formula at oshb:Ezek.5.5, and the samekh marks after 5:6 and 5:7 stand before the messenger formulae at oshb:Ezek.5.7 and oshb:Ezek.5.8; each of those three verses is one of the 122 verses carrying the long messenger formula, and each carries it verse-initially, 5:7 behind לָכֵ֞ן (oshb:Ezek.5.7) and 5:8 behind לָכֵ֗ן (oshb:Ezek.5.8). The remaining two do not: oshb:Ezek.5.10 opens on לָכֵ֗ן with no messenger formula, and oshb:Ezek.5.11 opens on the oath with the utterance signature attached mid-verse. No one of the five is read as a unit-cutting seam, and the reason is not any absence of coincidence but the condition such a cut needs: not one of them follows a verse that ENDS on a close-role formula, since none of 5:4, 5:6, 5:7, 5:9 or 5:10 carries an utterance formula or belongs to the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), and a parashah mark by itself cannot license the cut. Single witness: a pe stands after MT 4:17, the mark this witness sets at the seam where this unit begins.

P02-002.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.7 וַיָּבֵ֥א אֹתִ֖י אֶל פֶּ֣תַח הֶֽחָצֵ֑ר וָאֶרְאֶ֕ה וְהִנֵּ֥ה חֹר אֶחָ֖ד בַּקִּֽיר — a fresh transport (“He brought me to the door of the court” (web:Ezek.8.7), sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences) opens a new tableau, paired with the “Son of man, dig now in the wall” (web:Ezek.8.8) command at oshb:Ezek.8.8. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.13 וַיֹּ֖אמֶר אֵלָ֑י ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה תּוֹעֵב֥וֹת גְּדֹל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר הֵ֥מָּה עֹשִֽׂים repeats the “you will again see” (web:Ezek.8.6) transition that also closed the unit ending at Ezek.8.6, signalling the end of the elders'-idolatry tableau (Jaazaniah and the seventy elders censing before wall-carvings 'in the dark,' saying “Yahweh doesn’t see us” (web:Ezek.8.12)) and the turn to the next abomination. Both sides: a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.8.6 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to the seam behind it, even though the onset verse itself is a clean transport with no competing formula; the close has no Masoretic mark at all (no pe or samekh follows 8:13) and rests solely on the repeated 'again see' device, which is disclosed as weaker, tier-4-adjacent evidence rather than a refrain-grade close.
P02-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending this row through 8:18 (treating the three remaining temple-tour tableaux as one row) was weighed: the text supports it by the repeated 'again see' device running through 8:6, 8:13 and 8:15, but a twelve-verse row (MEASURED: web:Ezek.8.7-Ezek.8.18 is 12 verses, counted on the WEB face) with no internal formula anchor at all would understate the three distinct transport-marked scenes; the transport verbs at 8:7, 8:14 and 8:16 are kept as row-opening evidence instead.

P02-018.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.17 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל בְּנ֣וֹת עַמְּךָ֔ הַמִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וֹת מִֽלִּבְּהֶ֑ן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽן — “set your face against the daughters of your people” (web:Ezek.13.17) — is one of the book's 9 set-your-face verses and marks an addressee-class shift from the male prophets of 13:1-16 to women “who prophesy out of their own heart” (web:Ezek.13.17). Close: oshb:Ezek.13.23 לָכֵ֗ן שָׁ֚וְא לֹ֣א תֶחֱזֶ֔ינָה וְקֶ֖סֶם לֹא תִקְסַ֣מְנָה ע֑וֹד וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י אֶת עַמִּי֙ מִיֶּדְכֶ֔ן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ן כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends “Then you will know that I am Yahweh.” (web:Ezek.13.23) in the second-feminine-plural form (וידעתן), a counted form of its own (sweep: 2 verses) that belongs to neither the 3mp-28 nor the 2mp-21 recognition family, yet stands, like the matching 2fp clause that closes the magic-bands sub-paragraph at oshb:Ezek.13.21, in the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), any member of which is refrain-grade close evidence. Both sides: a pe follows oshb:Ezek.13.16 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness); the onset itself is tier-1 (set-your-face, address-class shift); the close is refrain-grade, a wide-family member in the two-verse 2fp form though in neither the 3mp nor the 2mp form; no parashah mark falls exactly at 13:23 (single-witness), and the row is held at medium rather than high confidence.
P02-018.device_notes: The two 2fp recognition clauses at 13:21 and 13:23 are a counted form of their own (sweep: 2 verses), and these two verses are its whole membership; the form is kept apart from the 3mp family (sweep: 28 verses) and the 2mp family (sweep: 21 verses) and is not added to either; both verses are nonetheless members of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses). P06-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — a year-and-day dateline whose month is not named (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after. Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit.

P09-002.device_notes: Category disclosure: the 37.15-28 span is anchored as sign_act (the commanded stick action of 37.16-20), but its interpretation at 37.21-28 carries the salvation_oracle burden (gather/return, the covenant of peace at 37.26, ‘my servant David’ and ‘my sanctuary’ devices) -- a one-clause category deviation rather than a split: the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28 are the row's only framing marks, and the addressee stays constant across both halves. 37.16 is a doubled ketiv/qere verse: two notes on one verse, each written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.16, ketiv), and each read as the same consonantal word under different pointing -- the first note reads חֲבֵרָ֑יו and the second חֲבֵרָֽיו, the two differing by exactly one codepoint, U+0591 HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA in the first against U+05BD HEBREW POINT METEG in the second (MEASURED by comparing the two readings the K/Q apparatus gives at this verse, codepoint by codepoint; WLC/OSHB, single witness), and 37.19 carries one further note on the same word (written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, ketiv), read חֲבֵרָ֑יו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, Qere)); 37.22 carries a further K/Q note in this span (written יהיה (oshb:Ezek.37.22, ketiv), read יִֽהְיוּ (oshb:Ezek.37.22, Qere)). A boundary is never argued from any of these Qere readings; they are disclosed as textual-variant sites only.

P10-001.device_notes: Chapters 40-42 carry none of the book's 184 parashah occurrences; the preceding pe at oshb:Ezek.39.29 (single-witness) is the nearest mark, on the verse this row's onset immediately follows. P10-011.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:15 opens with the completion notice וְכִלָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.15) “when he had finished measuring the inner house” (web:Ezek.42.15) -- a close-grade formula pressed into onset service here, since it explicitly marks the end of the inner-house survey that has run since 40:5 before turning outward to the perimeter wall -- paired with the transport verb וְהוֹצִיאַ֨נִי֙ 'he brought me out', which makes 42:15 a verse of the counted guided-motion class (sweep: 33 verses / 46 occurrences) and gives the onset a licensed driver inside the vision. Four cardinal-direction measurements follow (east 42:16, north 42:17, south 42:18, west 42:19), each opening with a measure verb on its own line, then a summary at 42:20. Close side: 42:20 ends on the wall's purpose, לְהַבְדִּ֕יל בֵּ֥ין הַקֹּ֖דֶשׁ לְחֹֽל (oshb:Ezek.42.20) “to make a separation between that which was holy and that which was common” (web:Ezek.42.20) -- a genuine thematic close, and the point at which the whole measuring circuit that opened at 40:5 ends, immediately before 43:1's transport verb and the glory's return open a new kind of scene. Both sides of this seam are unusually well aligned: a completion-formula onset and a purpose-clause close on one side, a transport-plus-glory onset on the other.

P11-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at 47.5/47.6 to isolate the measuring circuit (47.3-5) as its own temple_measurement row. It is weighed and held on stated grounds. The rival's near face, Ezek.47.6, IS licensed: the verse is both a said-to-me verse and a guided-motion verse (וַיּוֹלִכֵ֥נִי, וַיְשִׁבֵ֖נִי), and it is a transport verse of the counted class (sweep: 33 verses), so a seam there would not be device-free. Its far face, Ezek.47.5, carries the fourth measure-verb occurrence and a content close (נַ֖חַל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא יֵעָבֵֽר), with no close-role formula and no parashah mark, so the rival is one-faced rather than two-faced. The row holds against it on three stated grounds: Ezek.47.6's question looks BACK at the measuring just reported and its motion returns the prophet to the bank inside one scene rather than opening a new one; 47:1-12 reads as a single region with 47:6 inside it as interior texture; and the only further signal at 47:6 is the WEB's mid-verse paragraph, which is tier-4 and never corroborates a seam. Guided-motion verbs stand inside the measuring circuit, though not at its head: MEASURED over the pointed Hebrew witness, Ezek.47.3 does not BEGIN with a guided-motion verb (it opens בְּצֵאת הָאִ֥ישׁ) but does carry וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי later in the verse, and Ezek.47.4 carries that same form twice. Both verses are members of the same counted class, standing inside the measuring circuit, weighed and not taken, since each of those verbs steps the prophet one wading further after a measuring of a thousand cubits rather than opening a new scene. The measuring sequence therefore remains texture inside the single river vision running 47.1-12, disclosed as a one-sentence category deviation rather than split into a separate row (oshb:Ezek.47.5, oshb:Ezek.47.3, oshb:Ezek.47.6).
P11-010.device_notes: Category deviation, disclosed: this row's span briefly carries temple_measurement's own device (the four measured wadings, 47.3-5) inside an otherwise vision_report unit; disclosed in this one sentence rather than split into a separate row, since no formula bounds 47.3-5 off on either side. Inside that circuit two further rival onsets were weighed and not taken: a cut before MT 47:3 would rest on its guided-motion verb וַיַּעֲבִרֵ֥נִי (oshb:Ezek.47.3), which stands mid-verse after the man's first measuring, against a far face at 47:2 that ends on the water seen flowing at the right with no close formula and no section mark (single-witness), and it would leave 47:1-2 as a two-verse row, which is not the complete word-event unit a row that short requires; a cut before MT 47:4 would fall where both of that verse's guided-motion verbs follow a measure verb, inside the second and third of the four measured wadings, and would divide one measuring sequence whose far face, 47:3, ends on ankle-deep water with no close-role formula. Ezek.47.12 carries the construction glossed 'its months', the last of the book's chodesh-root homographs, disclosed as NOT a date formula.
